id.content:
/-- An induction (or recursion) principle for any type with a position function.
`C` is the *motive* of the recursion. If we can produce `C x` given `C y` for all `y` with position
lower than `x`, we can produce `C x` for all `x`. -/
@[elab_as_elim]
def pos_induction {X : Type _} [Position X] {C : X → Sort _} (x : X)
    (h : ∀ x, (∀ y, pos y < pos x → C y) → C x) : C x :=
  WellFounded.induction (InvImage.wf pos (inferInstanceAs <| IsWellFounded μ (· < ·)).wf) x h

`C` is the *motive* of the recursion. If we can produce `C x` given `C y` for all `y` with position
lower than `x`, we can produce `C x` for all `x`. -/

  WellFounded.induction (InvImage.wf pos (inferInstanceAs <| IsWellFounded μ (· < ·)).wf) x h

C1_dependencies.name: inferInstanceAs
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- `inferInstanceAs α` synthesizes a value of any target type by typeclass
inference. This is just like `inferInstance` except that `α` is given
explicitly instead of being inferred from the target type. It is especially
useful when the target type is some `α'` which is definitionally equal to `α`,
but the instance we are looking for is only registered for `α` (because
typeclass search does not unfold most definitions, but definitional equality
does.) Example:
```
#check inferInstanceAs (Inhabited Nat) -- Inhabited Nat
```
-/
abbrev inferInstanceAs (α : Sort u) [i : α] : α := i
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:
/-- `inferInstanceAs α` synthesizes a value of any target type by typeclass
inference. This is just like `inferInstance` except that `α` is given
explicitly instead of being inferred from the target type. It is especially
useful when the target type is some `α'` which is definitionally equal to `α`,
but the instance we are looking for is only registered for `α` (because
typeclass search does not unfold most definitions, but definitional equality
does.) Example:
```
#check inferInstanceAs (Inhabited Nat) -- Inhabited Nat
```
-/
abbrev inferInstanceAs (α : Sort u) [i : α] : α := i
